Polarity is correct if

Introduction
This document outlines the testing procedures P1, 
 which must be carried out 
 every two years as indicated by Y2 in the

Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff 
 should carry the suitable safety category.
Maintenance staff should be well trained, qualified or

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Caution:

Polarity Test Procedures
Move test 
 selector switch to SEC/10 +PRI position.
Refer to the figure 
 of test connections.
Verify that the 
 power ON/OFF switch is OFF. connect the test set to a suitable source of power 
 (as indicated on the nameplate) and ground.
Connect the test 
 set secondary out put binding posts X1 and X2 to secondary of current 
 transformer X1 and X2.observe polarity marks on the CT( X1 on the CTER-91 is 
 polarity).
Connect the test 
 set primary binding posts H1 and H2 to CT primary bushings H1 and H2 observe 
 polarity marks (H1 on the CTER-91 is polarity).
Turn power ON/OFF 
 switch to ON
Slowly increase 
 OUT PUT control to a known voltage.
Switch the RUN/ 
 HOLD switch to HOLD .return out put control to zero .read and record the 
 values.
Return RUN /HOLD switch to RUN.
 Polarity is correct if the primary voltmeter indicates the secondary voltage 
 being applied divided by ten plus voltage feeding back from the primary. For 
 example, using a 200:1 transformer excited to 200 volts, the primary voltmeter 
 would read 21 volts.
Note 1:
When working with 
 transformers where the meter indication only changes by a small fraction, it 
 is suggested that the user also perform a polarity test with SEC /10-PRI 
 (using the method described above ).this will give the user a second 
 opportunity to validate the polarity.
Polarity is correct if 
 the primary voltmeter indicates the secondary voltage being applied divided by 
 ten minus voltage feeding back from the primary. Voltmeter would read 19 
 volts.
Note 2:
For larger 
 transformers, the SEC /100+PRI would be more applicable. The procedure 
 would remain the same except substitute SEC /100+PRI where appropriate.
